title: Separate equilibrium spring energy from prepared work and reset
statement: For a linear port with free gap delta0, compliance R>0 and an attached zero-rest spring k>=0, delta=delta0/(1+k*R) gives stored spring energy E_k=k*delta0^2/[2*(1+k*R)^2]. Its maximum is delta0^2/(8*R) at k=1/R when delta0!=0. The port potential Phi(delta)=(delta-delta0)^2/(2*R)+constant drops by delta0^2/(2*R) on the specified release from a constrained delta=0 state to free delta0 at fixed boundaries. A port already relaxed at delta0 has no such releasable drop without a newly paid preparation or changed drive.

requires: R>0,k>=0 and the stated quasistatic zero-rest-spring port; fixed boundary displacement/geometry while evaluating equilibrium.
For work release, an actual initial constraint delta=0, subsequent release toward delta0 and paid preparation/loading/reset. A freely relaxed initial state does not satisfy this premise.

assumptions: Stored spring energy is not a proof of a feasible valve, coupling/release path or repeatable harvesting cycle.
The near-balance asymptotic uses the specified symmetric linear bridge at fixed K0,Delta; it is not a universal passive-work bound under arbitrary driving.
costs: Pay loading, port constraint/latch, reset, capture/storage losses and required valve work. Levers trade stroke for force without creating work.
contract.units: delta,delta0,Delta are lengths; R length/force; k,K0 force/length; E,Phi work. d,e are dimensionless normalized stiffness/error.
contract.obstruction: Acquire the initial-state preparation and complete work/reset trajectory before treating a precision signal as powered actuation.

body: Differentiate E_k: dE_k/dk=delta0^2*(1-k*R)/[2*(1+k*R)^3]. The nonzero-gap optimum follows; if delta0=0 every k stores zero energy. The quadratic port potential follows by integrating the port potential gradient (delta-delta0)/R. Phi(0)-Phi(delta0)=delta0^2/(2*R) is a difference between specified states. Starting at the free minimum and pulling the port to0 instead costs that amount. Connecting/preloading a spring or driving the outer boundaries also requires an actual preparation path; a stationary matrix computation does not supply it. Thus the source label available_energy is not accepted as free work from an already relaxed comparator or as a universal bound under arbitrary boundary motion. A prepared zero-gap release can leave an optimized spring with one-quarter of that potential drop; neither that ratio nor the stationary stored energy certifies a complete actuator/reset cycle. In the source symmetric bridge a=b=c=K0,bottom=K0*d with K0>0,d>0, delta0=Delta*(1-d)/[2*(1+d)] and R=(3+d)/[2*K0*(1+d)]. For e=1-d near0 at fixed Delta,K0, delta0=Delta*e/4+O(e^2) and the conditional potential drop is K0*Delta^2*e^2/32+O(e^3). A fixed switching-work demand therefore needs separately charged energy, a prepared storage path or a vanishing-work actuator near balance. No cycle counts or source numerical table were replayed.
